Then He, exalted is He, mentioned that to Him belongs the unseen (*ghayb*) of the heavens and the earth, which is what is hidden from the servants and whose knowledge is concealed from them. The apparent connection is with His saying: ﴿Indeed, God knows and you do not know﴾ (al-Nahl: 74). He informed that He alone has the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and with perfect power to bring the Hour, which you deny, in the blink of an eye or even quicker. The meaning of this information is that the gods you worship lack these two attributes that belong to the deity: all-encompassing knowledge of the unseen, and absolute, complete power. Whoever says that His saying ﴿and who commands justice﴾ refers to God, exalted is He, mentions the connection of this sentence to what precedes it, namely that whoever commands justice, and who is on a straight path, is the perfect one in knowledge and power. This sentence clarifies that.

It has been said: "The unseen here is what cannot be perceived by the senses and cannot be grasped by the intellect." Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "What is hidden from creation is within His grasp and nothing escapes Him." It has also been said: it refers to what is in His saying: ﴿Indeed, with God is the knowledge of the Hour﴾ (Luqman: 34). Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or he meant by the unseen of the heavens and the earth the Day of Resurrection, in that its knowledge is hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, none of whom has come to know of it."

It has been said: since the Hour is coming without fail, it is brought close, like the blink of an eye. Al-Zajjaj said: "He did not mean that the Hour comes in the blink of an eye. He only described the speed of the power to bring it about, i.e., He says to a thing 'Be,' and it is." It has been said: this is an illustration of nearness, as you say: "A year is nothing but a moment." Al-Zamakhshari said: "It is near with God, even if it is delayed, as they say of the thing you consider near: ﴿like the blink of an eye or even nearer﴾ when you exaggerate in considering it near." Similar is His saying: ﴿and they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾ (al-ʿAnkabut: 53), ﴿and God will not break His promise﴾ (al-Hajj: 47), ﴿and indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (al-Hajj: 47), meaning: it is near to Him, while it is far from you.

It has been said: the meaning is that the establishment of the Hour, the causing of the living to die, and the raising of the dead from the first and the last, will occur in the nearest time He has willed.

﴿Indeed, God is over all things competent﴾ (al-ʿAnkabut: 20), so He is able to establish the Hour and resurrect creation, since that is among the things within His power. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning, according to Qatada and others, is: the Hour and its establishment are within God's power only when He says to it 'Be,' so if a human being happened to witness this, it would be so swift that he would doubt whether it was like the blink of an eye or nearer than that. So *aw*, in this case, is in its original sense of doubt. It has also been said that it is for choice." End of quotation.

Doubt and choice are both far-fetched, because this is an announcement from God, exalted is He, about the matter of the Hour, and doubt is impossible for Him. Also, choice occurs only in prohibited matters, like the saying: "Take from my wealth a dinar or a dirham," or in obligations, like the verse of expiations: ﴿And those who divorce by zihar﴾ (al-Mujadila: 3). *Aw* here is for obscuring the matter from the addressee, like His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ (al-Saffat: 147), and His saying: ﴿Our command came upon it by night or by day﴾ (Yunus: 24). God knows their number and when His command will come upon them, just as He knows the matter of the Hour, but it was obscured from the addressee. That *aw* here is for obscuring was mentioned by al-Zajjaj here. Al-Qadi said: "This is not valid, because the establishment of the Hour is not a state of obligation such that it could be said that He brings it at a time—meaning the Qadi's time—so that the obscuring would be from the addressee at that time, and it is not a time of obligation." What we say is: the obscuring occurred at the time of the preceding address concerning the matter of the Hour, not at the time of its coming. It is not a condition of obscuring from the addressee in reporting something that the time of the report and the time of that thing's occurrence be the same. Do you not see, in His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ (al-Saffat: 147), how the time of the report was later than the time of that sending and their existence as a hundred thousand or more?

Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: "'The blink of the eye' (*lamḥ al-baṣar*) is the movement of the body by the glance from the top of the pupil, and it is composed of parts, and those parts are numerous. The time in which the blink takes place is composed of successive moments, and God is able to establish the Resurrection in one of those moments. Therefore He said: ﴿or it is nearer﴾. Since the swiftest of states and events in our minds is the blink of the eye, He mentioned it, then said: 'or it is nearer,' as an alert to what we have mentioned. The intended meaning is not the manner of doubt; rather, the meaning is: 'Indeed, it is nearer.'" End of quotation, and there is some abridgement in it.

What he mentioned, that *aw* means *bal* (rather), is the view of al-Farra', and it is not valid, because the transition (*iḍrāb*) is of two kinds, and neither is valid here. The first: that it be a cancellation of the preceding predication, and that it was not what was intended. This is impossible here, because it would result in a predication that does not correspond. The second: that it be a transition from one thing to another without cancelling that preceding thing. This is also impossible here, because of the contradiction between reporting that it is like the blink of an eye in speed and reporting that it is nearer, so both cannot be true together.

The author of *al-Ghaniyyan* said: "Although this is hard to grasp literally, what is intended is exaggeration, according to the way of the Arabs and the masters of composition." How excellent is the saying of the poet al-Ablah on this meaning:

> The lightning said to him, and the wind said to him, both together, and they are what they are:
> "Do you run with us?" He said: "If I become energetic, I will make you both laugh at yourselves."
> "I am the return of the glance, I have outpaced it toward the goal in speed, so who are you two?"

When He, exalted is He, mentioned the matter of the Hour and that it is certainly coming, this indicated the Hereafter's creation. The earlier description of them with the absence of knowledge was mentioned, so He mentioned the first creation, which is bringing them out from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, as an alert to the occurrence of the later creation. Then He mentioned His favor upon them in giving them the senses, which are the means of perceiving things and attaining knowledge. Since the first creation was mentioned, and He made what they know by as one of the greatest blessings upon them, He said: ﴿so that you may give thanks﴾. The discussion of *ummahat* (mothers) was mentioned in al-Nisa'.

Hamza read with a kasra on the hamza and the mim here, and in al-Nur, al-Zumar and al-Najm, and al-Kisa'i read with a kasra on the hamza in them. Al-A'mash read with deletion of the hamza and a kasra on the mim, and Ibn Abi Layla read with its deletion and a fatha on the mim. Abu Hatim said: "Deleting the hamza is bad, but the reading of Ibn Ubayy is more correct." End of quotation. It was more correct because the kasra on the mim occurs only to assimilate it to the vowel of the hamza; when the hamza is deleted, the assimilation disappears. By contrast, Ibn Abi Layla's reading leaves the mim on its own vowel.

*Lā taʿlamūna* ("you do not know") is a circumstantial clause (*jumla ḥāliyya*), meaning: "while not knowing." It has been said: "You do not know anything of what the covenant taken from you in the loins of your fathers was, or anything of what was decreed for you of happiness or misery, or anything of your benefits." The more appropriate is the general sense of the word "anything," especially in the context of negation. Wahb said: "The child is born wary for seven days; he does not perceive comfort or pain." It is possible that *wajaʿala* (and He made) is conjoined to ﴿He brought you out﴾, so it is one part within the scope of the predicate of the subject; and it is possible that it is a new statement conjoined to the initial sentence, like the beginning of it.

The meaning of the hearing, the sights and the hearts is their sensing and perceiving, so the faculty is expressed by the organ. Abu Abdullah al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din al-Razi) said, in substance: "The reason the word *fu'ad* (heart) is given in the paucity plural (*jam' qilla*, the plural form for small numbers) is that it was created only for true, certain knowledge, whereas most people are preoccupied with bestial acts, so their hearts are not really hearts. For this reason the paucity plural is used for it." End of his words, summarized. This is a delirious statement. Were it not for the eminence of the one who said it and his having written it in books, I would not have mentioned it. What should be said about this is what al-Zamakhshari said: that *afida* is among the paucity plurals that have come to function like plurals of abundance and paucity alike, when no other form of it is attested in usage, as with *shusu'* (the plural of *shis'*, "sandal-thong") which has no other plural form. So it follows that pattern. End of his words. However, al-Zamakhshari's claim that no plural of *shis'* other than *shusu'* occurs is not correct. A paucity plural also occurs for it: they say *ash-sa'* (*ashsa'*). So he should have said: "*shusu'* has been given precedence (as the common plural)."

Ibn Amir, Hamza, Talha, al-A'mash and Ibn Hurmuz read *alam tarawa* (ﷺ not applicable) with the second person "you" (*ta'* of address), while the rest of the seven readers read it with *ya'* (third person). Ibn Atiyya said: "There is a difference of report from al-Hasan, Isa al-Thaqafi, Asim and Abu Amr."

When the Exalted mentioned the three means of knowledge, hearing, sight and reason, the first two being the means of perceiving the sensible and the third the means of perceiving the intelligible, He confined the mention of the means of perceiving the sensible to sight, since it is the most striking for what is observed by it of the great creatures at their varied distances, such as observing the luminous bodies in the spheres. He placed the flying animal as the object of consideration and wonder here, for its flight in the air despite the weight of its body is among the things that cause wonder and are taken as a lesson. The verse also includes mention of the means of perceiving by reason, in that the bird does not fall, since there is nothing beneath it to support it and nothing above it to which it is attached. Thus reason knows that there is a holder of it who is able to hold it up, and He is God the Exalted, as the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is Seer of all things.﴾ (67:19). Thus the verse brings together the mention of the means of sense perception and the means of reasoning.

The meaning of *musakhkharat* ("made subservient") is "made pliable," and it is in the passive form to indicate that it has a subjector. Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: "This is evidence of the perfection of God's power and wisdom, for He the Exalted created the bird with a form by which flight is possible for it. He gave it a wing that it spreads at one time and folds at another, like what the swimmer does in water. He created the air with a form by which flight is possible. He created it in a subtle form by which piercing and passing through it is easy. Were it not for that, flight would not be possible." End of his words. His statement is drawn from the words of al-Qadi, who said: "He attributed the holding to Himself because He is the one who gave the instruments, for the sake of which the bird was able to perform those actions. Since He is the one who causes that, this attribution is valid." End of his words.

What we say is that the bird could have flown even had no wing been created for it, and it could have pierced a dense object by the power of God the Exalted (p-523), and the one who holds it in the atmosphere of the sky is God the Exalted. Proof has been established that all actions are created by God, and proof has been established that He the Exalted is the Doer who chooses. So we do not say: "Were it not for the wing and the subtlety of the air, flight would not be possible, and were it not for the instruments, it would not be possible."

Al-Zamakhshari said, in agreement with their words: "*Musakhkharat*: made pliable for flight by what He created for them of wings and the suitable causes for that." Then he rightly concluded with his statement: "None holds them up in their gripping and spreading and standing except God by His power." End of his words.

*La-ayat* ("indeed signs"): it is in the plural and not the singular, because the signs in it include the lightness of the bird which God placed in it so that it may rise by it, its weight which He placed in it so that it may descend, the space between the sky and the earth, and the holding which belongs to God the Exalted. Or it is plural in consideration of what is in this verse and the one before it. He said: *li-qawmin yu'minun* ("for a people who believe"), for they are those who benefit from consideration. And because the verse includes that the one who subjects them and holds them is God, this is a report from Him the Exalted which only the believer confirms.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 16, verses 80–83:**

﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest, and He has made for you, from the hides of the livestock, tents which you find light to carry on the day of your travelling and on the day of your settling, and from their wool, their fur and their hair, household goods and provision for a time.﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He created, shades, and He has made for you refuges in the mountains, and He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence. Thus He completes His favour upon you, that perhaps you may submit.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away, then your duty is only the clear conveyance.﴾ ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah, then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾

When He, exalted is He, mentioned what He had bestowed upon them of their creation, and what He had created for them of the faculties of knowledge, He mentioned what He had graciously bestowed upon them of the things that benefit them in their lives, from the external matters pertaining to their animals, namely the houses in which they dwell, made of stone, clay, wood and other materials.

*Al-sakan* (a place of rest, from *sakana*, to be at rest) is a *fa'al* form in the sense of a *maf'ul* (object), like *al-qansi* and *al-naqs*. Al-Farra' recited:

*Winter has come, and I have not taken a dwelling place;*
*Woe to my soul from digging the holes of the field mice!*

*Al-sakan* is not a verbal noun (*masdar*), as Ibn Atiyya held. It seems that He, exalted is He, first mentioned what is characteristic of houses, namely that they do not move, but people move to them. Then He mentioned secondly what He had bestowed upon us of what is made from the hides of livestock, which is what moves, namely domes, tents and portable shelters made of leather. Alternatively, He first mentioned houses in general, then mentioned houses of hides specifically, as a notice of the condition of most of the Arabs, for because of their seasonal migrations (*intija'*), their houses are mostly of hides. Apparently, houses of hair and houses of wool and fur are not included among the houses made of the hides of livestock. Ibn Salam said they are included, because they are fixed in them, so they are from them.

The meaning of *tastakhhifunaha* (you find them light) is: you find them light to carry in striking (dismantling) and in moving.

Ibn Qutayba said: the shades of trees and mountains; the *aknan* (refuges) from the mountains are the caves, the hollows, and the houses hewn out of them.

*On a night of Jumada, with its dews,*

As for *tuslimun* in the recitation of the majority, the meaning is: you believe, or you are led to reflection on the favours of Allah, exalted is He, which leads to faith and submission.

﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest, and He has made for you, from the hides of the livestock, tents which you find light to carry on the day of your travelling and on the day of your settling, and from their wool, their fur and their hair, household goods and provision for a time.﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He created, shades, and He has made for you refuges in the mountains, and He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence. Thus He completes His favour upon you, that perhaps you may submit.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away, then your duty is only the clear conveyance.﴾ ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah, then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾

When He, exalted is He, mentioned what He had bestowed upon them of their creation, and what He had created for them of the faculties of knowledge, He mentioned what He had graciously bestowed upon them of the things that benefit them in their lives, from the external matters pertaining to their animals, namely the houses in which they dwell, made of stone, clay, wood and other materials.

*Al-sakan* (a place of rest, from *sakana*, to be at rest) is a *fa'al* form in the sense of a *maf'ul* (object), like *al-qansi* and *al-naqs*. Al-Farra' recited:

*Winter has come, and I have not taken a dwelling place;*
*Woe to my soul from digging the holes of the field mice!*

*Al-sakan* is not a verbal noun (*masdar*), as Ibn Atiyya held. It seems that He, exalted is He, first mentioned what is characteristic of houses, namely that they do not move, but people move to them. Then He mentioned secondly what He had bestowed upon us of what is made from the hides of livestock, which is what moves, namely domes, tents and portable shelters made of leather. Alternatively, He first mentioned houses in general, then mentioned houses of hides specifically, as a notice of the condition of most of the Arabs, for because of their seasonal migrations (*intija'*), their houses are mostly of hides. Apparently, houses of hair and houses of wool and fur are not included among the houses made of the hides of livestock. Ibn Salam said they are included, because they are fixed in them, so they are from them.

The meaning of *tastakhhifunaha* (you find them light) is: you find them light to carry in striking (dismantling) and in moving.

*Yawma za'nikum* (the day of your travelling): the day you journey, their carrying and transporting is light for you; and the day you halt and settle in a place, their striking is not heavy upon you. The lightness may also be intended for the two times of journey and residence, i.e., the period of seasonal migration and the period of settlement. Al-Haramayn and Abu 'Amr recited *z'anikim* with a fatha on the 'ayn, and the rest of the Seven recited it with a sukun on it; both are dialects. The sukun is not a lightening, as occurs in words like *al-sha'ar* and *al-sha'r* because of a throat letter (*harf al-halq*).

The apparent reading is that *athathan* (household goods) is an object, the sense being: and He made from their wool, their fur and their hair household goods. It has also been said that *athathan* is in the accusative of circumstance (*hal*), in the sense that the meaning is: He made from their wool, their fur and their hair houses; thus this would be coordinated with *min julud al-an'am* (from the hides of livestock), just as you say: "I made for you from water a drink and from milk [a drink]." According to the first reading, He has coordinated a genitive with a genitive and an accusative with an accusative, as you say: "I struck in the house Zayd and in the palace 'Amr." Since their lands were not lands of cotton, linen and silk, these three were restricted to here, and they were included in His words: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾.

*Al-mata'* is what is enjoyed, i.e., what is benefited from. Ibn 'Abbas said: adornment. Al-Mufaddal said: merchandise and livelihood. Al-Khalil said: *al-athath* and *al-mata'* are one thing, and He combined them because of the difference in wording, like His saying: ﴿and he found her word false and lying﴾.

He, exalted is He, limited that by His words: ﴿for a time﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: until death. Muqatil said: until that thing decays. It has also been said: until the end of your need for it.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned what He had graciously bestowed upon them, which has been mentioned before, and their lands were predominantly hot, He mentioned His favour upon them with what protects them from heat, namely the creation of bodies that have shade, such as trees and others that prevent the harm of the sun. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: the shades of clouds. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the shades of houses. Qatada and al-Zajjaj said: the shades of trees. Ibn Qutayba said: the shades of trees and mountains; the *aknan* (refuges) from the mountains are the caves, the hollows, and the houses hewn out of them.

*Al-sirbal* is what is worn on the body, of: a shirt, a *qarqal*, a *mijwal*, a coat of mail, a *jawshan*, and similar things, of wool, linen, cotton, or other materials. Mention was limited to the heat either because what protects from heat also protects from cold, as al-Zajjaj said, or because the opposite is omitted, as the opposite indicates it, as al-Mubarrad said, or because heat is more pressing in those lands, and cold is absent in most of them. When it comes, one protects oneself with household goods, so that the *sirbal* is reserved for protection from heat only, as 'Ata' al-Khurasani said. This is the case in the land of the Hijaz; as for other lands of the Arabs, severe cold is found there, as Mutammim said:

*When the crust from the cold of winter rattles.*

Another said:

*On a night of Jumada, with its dews,*
*and the garments which protect people are coats of mail.*

Ka'b ibn Zuhayr said:

*Lofty of noses, champions whose garments*
*are of the weaving of David, in battle, are coats of mail.*

*Al-sirbal* is general; it applies to what is of iron and other than iron. *Al-ba's* in the root of the language means severity, and here it means war. In a hadith: "When the battle grew fierce, we would seek protection by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The meaning is: it protects you from the harm of war, which is what occurs in it of wounds caused by the striking of the sword, the mace, the spear, the arrow, and other things prepared for combat.

*Kadhalika* (thus), i.e., like that completion of favour in the past, He will complete His favour in the future. Ibn 'Abbas recited *tatimmu* with an open *ta'*, and *ni'matuhu* with a *raf'* (nominative), attributing the completion to it, as an extension; and from him *ni'amuhu* in the plural. He recited *la'allakum taslamun* with a fatha on the *ta'* and the *lam*, from *al-salama* (safety) and deliverance, so it is as if it were a reason for the shielding of the garments from the harm of war, or "you are saved from polytheism." As for *tuslimun* in the recitation of the majority, the meaning is: you believe, or you are led to reflection on the favours of Allah, exalted is He, which leads to faith and submission.

It is reported that a Bedouin heard His saying: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest﴾ up to the end of the two verses, and he said at every favour: "O Allah, yes." When he heard: ﴿that perhaps you may submit﴾, he said: "O Allah, this is enough" (*fa-la*), so the verse ﴿But if they turn away﴾ was revealed.

It may be that *tawalla* is in the past tense, i.e., if they turn away from Islam. It may also be in the present tense, i.e., *fa-in tatawallaw*, with the *ta'* elided, and it would follow the previous address, and the past tense by way of *iltifat* (shift of person). The *fa'* and what follows it are the answer of the condition in form, while the true answer is omitted, i.e., you are excused, since you have fulfilled what was obligatory upon you. So the cause of the excuse, which is the conveyance, has been placed in the position of the thing caused, because it indicates it.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: The meaning is: if they turn away, you are not able to secure the truth of faith in their hearts; your duty is only to make clear and convey the command and prohibition of Allah; end of quotation.

Then He informed about them, as a rebuke and reproach, that they ﴿recognise the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾. Their recognition of the favours that were counted for them is when they acknowledge them and that they are from Him, exalted is He; and their denial of them is when they worship other than Allah. This denial is figurative, since they did not base upon knowledge of His favours the requirement of worshipping Him and devoting worship to Him alone, rather than those they associated with Him as partners. Mujahid said something close to this meaning. Al-Suddi said: the favour here is Muhammad ﷺ, and the meaning is: they recognise him through his miracles and the signs of his prophethood, and they deny that by denying him. Al-Tabari preferred this. It is also reported from Mujahid: their denial of their saying: "We inherited it from our fathers." It is reported from Ibn 'Awn: its attribution to the causes, not to the one who causes them. The author of al-Ghaniyyan reported: they recognise it in hardship, then deny it in ease. It has been said: their denial is by the intercession of their gods with Allah. It has been said: they recognise it with their hearts, then deny it with their tongues.

The apparent meaning is that what is intended by *wa-aktharuhum* (and most of them) is its original usage. Al-Hasan said: "and all of them": no one fulfils the obligation of the true gratitude, so he made it a denial of the favour. The apparent meaning is that disbelief here is the opposite of faith. It has been said: most of the people of Makkah, since among them were those who refused. It has been said: the meaning of *al-kafirun* (the disbelievers) is the obstinate deniers, since among them were those who were ignorant and did not know, so they did not obstinately deny. Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of *thumma* (then)? I say: it indicates that their denial is strange after the attainment of knowledge, since the one who knows the favour should acknowledge it, not deny it."

﴿On the Day We raise up from every nation a witness, then those who disbelieved will not be given leave, nor will they be allowed to make amends.﴾ ﴿When those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿When those who associated partners with God see their partners, they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You." But their partners will throw the word back at them: "Indeed you are liars."﴾ ﴿On that Day they will offer submission to God, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of God, We will increase their punishment, a punishment upon punishment, because of their corruption.﴾ ﴿On the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these people. And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾

When He mentioned their denial of God's blessing, He mentioned the state of the Day of Resurrection, in which denial will not benefit them, as a threat to them concerning that Day. The word (yawma) ("the Day") is governed by an implied (udhkur) ("remember"), as said by al-Hawfi, al-Zamakhshari, Ibn 'Atiyya and Abu al-Baqa'. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or (the meaning is): on the Day We raise up, they will fall into what they fell into." Al-Tabari said: it is conjoined to an omitted adverbial phrase whose governing element is ﴿then they deny it﴾ [al-Nahl: 83], meaning: they deny it today, and on the Day We raise up, meaning: they deny their disbelief, so the witness contradicts them. The witness (shahid) is the prophet of that nation, who bears witness against them concerning their faith and their disbelief. The object of the permission (idhn) is omitted. It has been said: it refers to returning to the abode of this world. It has been said: it refers to speech and making excuses, as He said: ﴿This is a Day on which they will not speak﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35] ﴿nor will they be given leave, so they will make no excuse﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36], meaning: after the testimony of their prophets against them. Otherwise, before that, every nation argues on behalf of itself. Their speech on this matter has been reported, but these are stations, in some of which they speak and in some of which they do not speak, "nor will they be allowed to make amends," meaning: the blame will be removed from them. Some people said: its meaning is that they will not ask to return to what they were upon in this world. So this is (istita'ab), whose meaning is seeking their pleasure (utba), and similar to it is the saying of one who said: "nor will they be asked to be pleased," meaning: it will not be said to them, "Please your Lord," because the Hereafter is not an abode of action, as said by al-Zamakhshari. Al-Tabari said: its meaning is that they will be given the opportunity to return to this world, so repentance and action will proceed from them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of this (thumma) ("then")? I say: its meaning is that after the testimony of the prophets they will be afflicted with something more severe than it, and that they will be prevented from speech, so they will not be given leave to offer an excuse or to present an argument." End of quotation. Since the state of punishment in this world differs from the state of the Hereafter, for whoever sees punishment in this world hopes to be delayed from it, and if he falls into it, hopes that it will be lightened for him, God, exalted is He, informed that the punishment of the Hereafter will admit of no lightening and no respite. The apparent view is that the response to (idha) ("when") is His saying ﴿it will not be lightened﴾, and it is with an implied (huwa) ("it"), meaning: "so it will not be lightened," because if the implied element were not assumed, the (fa') would not have entered, since when the response to (idha) is in the present tense it does not need the (fa'), whether affirmative or negative, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognise denial in the faces of those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Hajj: 72]. And you say: "When Zayd comes, 'Amr does not come." Al-Hawfi said: "so it will not be lightened" is the response to (idha), and it is what governs (idha). It has already been explained to us that what precedes the response-marking (fa') does not govern what comes before it, except in (amma), and we have explained that what governs (idha) is the verb that follows it, like the rest of the conditional particles, although this is not the view of the majority. Al-Zamakhshari made the response to (idha) omitted, saying: the governing element of (yawma nab'athu) is jussed, and he said: "On the Day We raise up, they will fall into what they fell into. Likewise, when they see the punishment, it will overtake them suddenly and will be heavy upon them, so it will not be lightened nor will they be reprieved," like His saying: ﴿Rather it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 40], to the end of the verse. End of quotation.

The apparent view is that His saying ﴿their partners﴾ is general, covering everyone they took as a partner to God, whether an idol, an image, a human, a devil, or an angel. Among them, whoever has reason will deny them, so the (fa-alqaw) ("they threw") refers to whoever possesses speech. It is also permissible that it be general, with God, exalted is He, causing the idols and images to speak by His power. The attribution of the partners to them, on this view, is because they are the ones who made them partners to God. Al-Hasan said: "Their partners are the devils, who shared with them in wealth and children," like His saying: ﴿and share with them in wealth and children﴾ [al-Isra': 64]. It has been said: their partners in disbelief. On the first view, (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they took them as gods alongside God and worshipped them), or (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they assigned for them a share of their wealth and livestock). The apparent view is that the speech is attributed to them literally. It has been said: it is attributed to their limbs, because when they denied associating partners by saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], God silenced their tongues and made their limbs speak. The meaning of (nad'u) ("we call upon") is (na'budu) ("we worship"). They said this hoping that they would share in the punishment with them, since that brings consolation, or as an excuse for their disbelief, since Satan adorned that for them and drove them to it, if the partners are the devils. Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: they said this to transfer this sin to those idols, supposing that this would save them from the punishment of God or from their own punishment. At that point, those idols will deny them. Al-Qadi said: this is far-fetched, because the disbelievers know by necessary knowledge in the Hereafter that the punishment will descend upon them, and that there is no help, no ransom, and no intercession. The report that they are partners had preceded, and the report that they used to call upon them, meaning worship them, had preceded. So the denial may refer to the first report, meaning: "we are not partners of God in worship, nor gods," and they exalt God above having partners. It may also refer to the second report, which is worship: since they were not content with worship, they regarded their worship as no worship, or since those [objects] did not call them to worship. Do you not see that idols and images have no awareness of being worshipped, let alone of calling anyone? And that whoever among the righteous believers and angels was worshipped did not call to his own worship? If the partners are devils, it is permissible that they be liars in their report about the falsity of those who worshipped them, just as Iblis lied in his saying: ﴿I disown what you associated with me before﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

The pronoun in (fa-alqaw ila Allah) ("they offered to God") refers to those who associated partners, as said by most. (Al-salam) means submission and compliance with God's judgment after refusal and arrogance in this world, so at that time they had no stratagem and no means of defence. Ya'qub related from Abu 'Amr: (al-silm) with a sukun on the lam. Mujahid recited it with a damma on the sin and the lam. It has been said: the pronoun refers to those who associated partners and all their partners together. Al-Kalbi said: they submitted, yielding to His judgment. The pronoun in (wa-dalla) ("and vanished") refers specifically to those who associated partners, meaning: what they used to fabricate has vanished from them, namely that God has partners and that those [partners] would help them and intercede for them, when those [partners] denied them and disowned them. The apparent view is that (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'), and (zidnahum) is the predicate (khabar). Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that (alladhina) is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in (yaftarun), and (zidnahum) is a new verb whose information is independent.

﴿And who barred others from the way of God﴾: meaning, others besides themselves. We will increase them in punishment because of the barring, a punishment upon punishment, meaning: the punishment that was due to them for disbelief. They doubled their disbelief, so God doubled their punishment. This increase is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as scorpions like tall palm trees, and from him as serpents like elephants and scorpions like mules. From Ibn 'Abbas: that it is molten brass flowing from beneath the Throne, with which they are punished. From al-Zajjaj: they will pass from the heat of Hell to the zamharir (extreme cold), and then they will hasten, because of its intense cold, back to Hell. He explained that increase by their causing others to go astray and inciting them to disbelief.

In each nation: the word (min-hā) ("from it") is omitted in the earlier (ayah), and it is affirmed here; and it is omitted there and affirmed here. The meaning in both is that God raises up the prophets of the nations, from among them, and the address in that is to the Messenger ﷺ, and the indication by ﴿these people﴾ is to his community. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that God raises up witnesses from among the righteous alongside the messengers. Some of the Companions have said: "If you see someone committing a sin, forbid him; if he obeys you, well and good, but if not, you will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection." End of quotation. The witness was "from among themselves" because he was so when he was sent to them in this world, from among themselves. Al-Asamm Abu Bakr said: the meaning of the witness is that God makes ten parts of the human being speak until they bear witness against him, because He said concerning the witness: "from among themselves." This is far-fetched, because it is contrasted with His saying: ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these people﴾, so the contrast requires that the witnesses over the nations be their prophets, like the Messenger of God ﷺ.

﴿And We have sent down﴾: this is a resumption of information, and it is not included with what precedes it, because the two times differ. When He mentioned what God honoured him with, namely witnessing over his community, He mentioned what was sent down to him, in which is the clarification of everything in the matters of religion, so as to remove thereby their excuse concerning what they were charged with, so that there is no proof or excuse for them.

The apparent view is that (tibyanan) is a verbal noun (masdar) of the form (tifal), though the general pattern of verbal nouns is to come as (taf'al) with a fatha, like (al-tardad) and (al-tawaf), and the analogue of (tibyan) in the kasra of its taa' is (tilqa'). Al-Zajjaj permitted its fatha outside the Qur'an. Ibn 'Atiyya said: (tibyanan) is a noun and not a verbal noun, and this is the view of most grammarians. Tha'lab related from the Kufans, and al-Mubarrad from the Basrans, that it is a verbal noun, and that among verbal nouns only two come in the form tifal: tibyan and tilqa'.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: how was the Qur'an an explanation of everything? I say: the meaning is that it clarified everything of the matters of religion, since it contained an explicit statement on some of them and a referral to the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition), since in it he was commanded to follow the Messenger of God ﷺ and obey him. It has been said: ﴿and he does not speak out of desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3], and an incitement to consensus (ijma') in His saying: ﴿and follows a path other than that of the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 115], and the Messenger of God ﷺ approved for his community following his Companions and imitating their footsteps in his saying: 'My Companions are like the stars: whichever of them you follow, you will be guided.' They strove, analysed, and laid down the paths of analogy (qiyas) and independent reasoning (ijtihad), so the Sunnah, the consensus, analogy and independent reasoning were all grounded in the clarification of the Book, and therefore it was an explanation of everything." His saying "and the Messenger of God ﷺ approved" up to "you will be guided" — the Messenger of God ﷺ did not say that; it is a fabricated hadith that is not authentic in any way from the Messenger of God ﷺ. The memorizer Abu Muhammad 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Hazm said in his treatise refuting opinion (ra'y), analogy, juristic preference (istihsan), causal reasoning (ta'lil), and imitation (taqlid), the following text: "This report is a lie, fabricated, and false; it has never been valid." He mentioned its chain to al-Bazzar, author of the Musnad, who said: "You asked about what is reported from the Prophet ﷺ, which is among the common people, narrating from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: 'The likeness of my Companions is only like the likeness of the stars, or like the stars; whichever of them they follow, they will be guided.' This speech is not authentic from the Prophet ﷺ. It was narrated by 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-'Ammi, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ. The weakness of this hadith comes from 'Abd al-Rahim, since the scholars refrained from narrating his hadith. The speech is also reprehensible from the Prophet ﷺ and is not established, and the Prophet ﷺ does not permit disagreement after him among his Companions." This is the text of al-Bazzar's speech. Ibn Ma'in said: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd is a great liar, wicked, and worthless. Al-Bukhari said: he is abandoned (matruk). It was also narrated by Hamzah al-Jazari, and this Hamzah is discarded and abandoned.

They made ﴿tibyanan﴾ a circumstantial accusative (hal). It is also permissible that it be an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi). And (lil-muslimin) is connected to (wa-busha) ("and good tidings"), while in meaning it is connected to "and guidance and mercy."

But their partners will throw the word back at them: "Indeed you are liars."﴾ ﴿On that Day they will offer submission to God, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of God, We will increase their punishment, a punishment upon punishment, because of their corruption.﴾ ﴿On the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these people. And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾

The apparent view is that His saying ﴿their partners﴾ is general, covering everyone they took as a partner to God, whether an idol, an image, a human, a devil, or an angel. The attribution of the partners to them, on this view, is because they are the ones who made them partners to God. It has been said: their partners in disbelief. On the first view, (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they took them as gods alongside God and worshipped them), or (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they assigned for them a share of their wealth and livestock). The apparent view is that the speech is attributed to them literally. It has been said: it is attributed to their limbs, because when they denied associating partners by saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], God silenced their tongues and made their limbs speak. Al-Qadi said: this is far-fetched, because the disbelievers know by necessary knowledge in the Hereafter that the punishment will descend upon them, and that there is no help, no ransom, and no intercession. (Al-salam) means submission and compliance with God's judgment after refusal and arrogance in this world, so at that time they had no stratagem and no means of defence. It has been said: the pronoun refers to those who associated partners and all their partners together. Al-Kalbi said: they submitted, yielding to His judgment. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that (alladhina) is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in (yaftarun), and (zidnahum) is a new verb whose information is independent.

﴿And who barred others from the way of God﴾: meaning, others besides themselves. They doubled their disbelief, so God doubled their punishment. This increase is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as scorpions like tall palm trees, and from him as serpents like elephants and scorpions like mules. He explained that increase by their causing others to go astray and inciting them to disbelief.

The meaning in both is that God raises up the prophets of the nations, from among them, and the address in that is to the Messenger ﷺ, and the indication by ﴿these people﴾ is to his community. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that God raises up witnesses from among the righteous alongside the messengers. Some of the Companions have said: "If you see someone committing a sin, forbid him; if he obeys you, well and good, but if not, you will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Asamm Abu Bakr said: the meaning of the witness is that God makes ten parts of the human being speak until they bear witness against him, because He said concerning the witness: "from among themselves." This is far-fetched, because it is contrasted with His saying: ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these people﴾, so the contrast requires that the witnesses over the nations be their prophets, like the Messenger of God ﷺ.

The witness (shahid) is the prophet of that nation, who bears witness against them concerning their faith and their disbelief. The object of the permission (idhn) is omitted. It has been said: it refers to returning to the abode of this world. It has been said: it refers to speech and making excuses, as He said: ﴿This is a Day on which they will not speak﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35] ﴿nor will they be given leave, so they will make no excuse﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36], meaning: after the testimony of their prophets against them. The apparent view is that the response to (idha) ("when") is His saying ﴿it will not be lightened﴾, and it is with an implied (huwa) ("it"), meaning: "so it will not be lightened," because if the implied element were not assumed, the (fa') would not have entered, since when the response to (idha) is in the present tense it does not need the (fa'), whether affirmative or negative, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognise denial in the faces of those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Hajj: 72]. And you say: "When Zayd comes, 'Amr does not come." Al-Hawfi said: "so it will not be lightened" is the response to (idha), and it is what governs (idha). It has already been explained to us that what precedes the response-marking (fa') does not govern what comes before it, except in (amma), and we have explained that what governs (idha) is the verb that follows it, like the rest of the conditional particles, although this is not the view of the majority. Al-Zamakhshari made the response to (idha) omitted, saying: the governing element of (yawma nab'athu) is jussed, and he said: "On the Day We raise up, they will fall into what they fell into. Likewise, when they see the punishment, it will overtake them suddenly and will be heavy upon them, so it will not be lightened nor will they be reprieved," like His saying: ﴿Rather it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 40], to the end of the verse. End of quotation.

The apparent view is that His saying ﴿their partners﴾ is general, covering everyone they took as a partner to God, whether an idol, an image, a human, a devil, or an angel. Among them, whoever has reason will deny them, so the (fa-alqaw) ("they threw") refers to whoever possesses speech. It is also permissible that it be general, with God, exalted is He, causing the idols and images to speak by His power. The attribution of the partners to them, on this view, is because they are the ones who made them partners to God. Al-Hasan said: "Their partners are the devils, who shared with them in wealth and children," like His saying: ﴿and share with them in wealth and children﴾ [al-Isra': 64]. It has been said: their partners in disbelief. On the first view, (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they took them as gods alongside God and worshipped them), or (their partners) refers to [their partners in] (that they assigned for them a share of their wealth and livestock). The apparent view is that the speech is attributed to them literally. It has been said: it is attributed to their limbs, because when they denied associating partners by saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], God silenced their tongues and made their limbs speak. The meaning of (nad'u) ("we call upon") is (na'budu) ("we worship"). They said this hoping that they would share in the punishment with them, since that brings consolation, or as an excuse for their disbelief, since Satan adorned that for them and drove them to it, if the partners are the devils. Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: they said this to transfer this sin to those idols, supposing that this would save them from the punishment of God or from their own punishment. At that point, those idols will deny them. Al-Qadi said: this is far-fetched, because the disbelievers know by necessary knowledge in the Hereafter that the punishment will descend upon them, and that there is no help, no ransom, and no intercession. The report that they are partners had preceded, and the report that they used to call upon them, meaning worship them, had preceded. So the denial may refer to the first report, meaning: "we are not partners of God in worship, nor gods," and they exalt God above having partners. It may also refer to the second report, which is worship: since they were not content with worship, they regarded their worship as no worship, or since those [objects] did not call them to worship. Do you not see that idols and images have no awareness of being worshipped, let alone of calling anyone? And that whoever among the righteous believers and angels was worshipped did not call to his own worship? If the partners are devils, it is permissible that they be liars in their report about the falsity of those who worshipped them, just as Iblis lied in his saying: ﴿I disown what you associated with me before﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

The pronoun in (fa-alqaw ila Allah) ("they offered to God") refers to those who associated partners, as said by most. (Al-salam) means submission and compliance with God's judgment after refusal and arrogance in this world, so at that time they had no stratagem and no means of defence. Ya'qub related from Abu 'Amr: (al-silm) with a sukun on the lam. Mujahid recited it with a damma on the sin and the lam. It has been said: the pronoun refers to those who associated partners and all their partners together. Al-Kalbi said: they submitted, yielding to His judgment. The pronoun in (wa-dalla) ("and vanished") refers specifically to those who associated partners, meaning: what they used to fabricate has vanished from them, namely that God has partners and that those [partners] would help them and intercede for them, when those [partners] denied them and disowned them. The apparent view is that (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'), and (zidnahum) is the predicate (khabar). Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that (alladhina) is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in (yaftarun), and (zidnahum) is a new verb whose information is independent.

﴿And who barred others from the way of God﴾: meaning, others besides themselves. We will increase them in punishment because of the barring, a punishment upon punishment, meaning: the punishment that was due to them for disbelief. They doubled their disbelief, so God doubled their punishment. This increase is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as scorpions like tall palm trees, and from him as serpents like elephants and scorpions like mules. From Ibn 'Abbas: that it is molten brass flowing from beneath the Throne, with which they are punished. From al-Zajjaj: they will pass from the heat of Hell to the zamharir (extreme cold), and then they will hasten, because of its intense cold, back to Hell. He explained that increase by their causing others to go astray and inciting them to disbelief.

In each nation: the word (min-hā) ("from it") is omitted in the earlier (ayah), and it is affirmed here; and it is omitted there and affirmed here. The meaning in both is that God raises up the prophets of the nations, from among them, and the address in that is to the Messenger ﷺ, and the indication by ﴿these people﴾ is to his community. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that God raises up witnesses from among the righteous alongside the messengers. Some of the Companions have said: "If you see someone committing a sin, forbid him; if he obeys you, well and good, but if not, you will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection." End of quotation. The witness was "from among themselves" because he was so when he was sent to them in this world, from among themselves. Al-Asamm Abu Bakr said: the meaning of the witness is that God makes ten parts of the human being speak until they bear witness against him, because He said concerning the witness: "from among themselves." This is far-fetched, because it is contrasted with His saying: ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these people﴾, so the contrast requires that the witnesses over the nations be their prophets, like the Messenger of God ﷺ.

﴿And We have sent down﴾: this is a resumption of information, and it is not included with what precedes it, because the two times differ. When He mentioned what God honoured him with, namely witnessing over his community, He mentioned what was sent down to him, in which is the clarification of everything in the matters of religion, so as to remove thereby their excuse concerning what they were charged with, so that there is no proof or excuse for them.

The apparent view is that (tibyanan) is a verbal noun (masdar) of the form (tifal), though the general pattern of verbal nouns is to come as (taf'al) with a fatha, like (al-tardad) and (al-tawaf), and the analogue of (tibyan) in the kasra of its taa' is (tilqa'). Al-Zajjaj permitted its fatha outside the Qur'an. Ibn 'Atiyya said: (tibyanan) is a noun and not a verbal noun, and this is the view of most grammarians. Tha'lab related from the Kufans, and al-Mubarrad from the Basrans, that it is a verbal noun, and that among verbal nouns only two come in the form tifal: tibyan and tilqa'.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: how was the Qur'an an explanation of everything? I say: the meaning is that it clarified everything of the matters of religion, since it contained an explicit statement on some of them and a referral to the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition), since in it he was commanded to follow the Messenger of God ﷺ and obey him. It has been said: ﴿and he does not speak out of desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3], and an incitement to consensus (ijma') in His saying: ﴿and follows a path other than that of the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 115], and the Messenger of God ﷺ approved for his community following his Companions and imitating their footsteps in his saying: 'My Companions are like the stars: whichever of them you follow, you will be guided.' They strove, analysed, and laid down the paths of analogy (qiyas) and independent reasoning (ijtihad), so the Sunnah, the consensus, analogy and independent reasoning were all grounded in the clarification of the Book, and therefore it was an explanation of everything." His saying "and the Messenger of God ﷺ approved" up to "you will be guided" — the Messenger of God ﷺ did not say that; it is a fabricated hadith that is not authentic in any way from the Messenger of God ﷺ. The memorizer Abu Muhammad 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Hazm said in his treatise refuting opinion (ra'y), analogy, juristic preference (istihsan), causal reasoning (ta'lil), and imitation (taqlid), the following text: "This report is a lie, fabricated, and false; it has never been valid." He mentioned its chain to al-Bazzar, author of the Musnad, who said: "You asked about what is reported from the Prophet ﷺ, which is among the common people, narrating from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: 'The likeness of my Companions is only like the likeness of the stars, or like the stars; whichever of them they follow, they will be guided.' This speech is not authentic from the Prophet ﷺ. It was narrated by 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-'Ammi, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ. The weakness of this hadith comes from 'Abd al-Rahim, since the scholars refrained from narrating his hadith. The speech is also reprehensible from the Prophet ﷺ and is not established, and the Prophet ﷺ does not permit disagreement after him among his Companions." This is the text of al-Bazzar's speech. Ibn Ma'in said: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd is a great liar, wicked, and worthless. Al-Bukhari said: he is abandoned (matruk). It was also narrated by Hamzah al-Jazari, and this Hamzah is discarded and abandoned.

They made ﴿tibyanan﴾ a circumstantial accusative (hal). It is also permissible that it be an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi). And (lil-muslimin) is connected to (wa-busha) ("and good tidings"), while in meaning it is connected to "and guidance and mercy."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 16, verses 90–92 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to close relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may remember.﴾ ﴿Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make a pledge, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, although you have made Allah your guarantor over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And do not be like her who unravels her yarn after it has been strong, into broken threads, taking your oaths as means of deceit between you, because one community is more numerous than another. Allah only tests you thereby, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ.﴾ ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 93] ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was firmly planted, and you taste evil for having averted [others] from the way of Allah, and you will have a great punishment.﴾ [An-Nahl: 94] ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. What is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [An-Nahl: 95] ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah remains. And We will surely reward those who were patient with the best of what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 96] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 97] ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.﴾ [An-Nahl: 98] ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.﴾ [An-Nahl: 99] ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾ [An-Nahl: 100] ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, "You are only a fabricator." But most of them do not know.﴾ [An-Nahl: 101] ﴿Say: "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to make firm those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."﴾ [An-Nahl: 102] ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [An-Nahl: 103]

Al-naqd is the opposite of al-ibram (tightening/firm twisting), and in the case of a body it means separating its parts from one another. Al-tawkid means confirmation and firming up; it is said tawkid and ta'kid, and both are two dialectal forms. al-Zajjaj claimed that the hamzah is a substitute for the waw, but this is not sound, because the morphological derivation occurs in both forms, which indicates that they are two original roots. Al-ghazl is well known; its verb is ghazala yaghzilu, with a kasra on the zay, ghazlan, and the verbal noun was applied to the thing spun. Nafida al-shay' yanfadu means it was exhausted, finished. Al-a'jami is one who does not speak Arabic. (p. 529)

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to close relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may remember.﴾ ﴿Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make a pledge, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, although you have made Allah your guarantor over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And do not be like her who unravels her yarn after it has been strong, into broken threads, taking your oaths as means of deceit between you, because one community is more numerous than another. Allah only tests you thereby, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ.﴾: From Ibn Abbas, in a lengthy narration: "Uthman ibn Maz'un was a companion of the Prophet ﷺ for a time, and he said to him: 'Uthman, I have not seen you do your act this morning?' He said: 'And what did you see me do?' He said: 'Your gaze was lifted toward the sky, then you placed it on your right, and you turned away from me toward it and left me. Then you began nodding your head as if you were understanding something being said to you.' He said: 'Did you notice that? The Messenger of Allah came to me just now while you were sitting.' He said: 'What did he say to you?' He said to me: '﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾,' the verse. Uthman said: 'That was the moment when faith settled in my heart, and I came to love Muhammad ﷺ.'"

When Allah mentioned ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ [An-Nahl: 89], He connected to it what requires obligations, whether obligatory, voluntary, moral, or behavioral. Al-'adl (justice) is the performance of every obligation concerning beliefs, laws, and conduct with people in the fulfillment of trusts, the abandonment of injustice, fairness, and the giving of rights. Al-ihsan (good conduct) is the performance of every recommended act. This was said by Ibn Atiyyah. al-Zamakhshari said: Al-'adl is the obligatory, because Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, was just in it toward His servants, making what He imposed on them fall within their capacity. Al-ihsan is the recommended, and its command was linked to them all, because an obligation must inevitably involve some shortcoming, which the recommended act compensates for; end of quote. In his statement "within their capacity" there is a trace of i'tizal (the Mu'tazila tendency). From Ibn Abbas: al-'adl is "There is no god but Allah," and al-ihsan is the performance of the obligatory duties. Also from him: al-'adl is the truth. From Sufyan ibn Uyaynah: it is the equality of inner and outer conduct in action. al-Mawardi mentioned that it is judging by the truth, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ [An-Nisa: 58]. Abu Sulayman said: al-'adl in the language of the Arabs is fairness. It was also said: it is the removal of rivals. It was said: al-'adl is in actions and al-ihsan is in words.

Giving to close relatives (iytaʾ dhi al-qurba) is maintaining family ties (silat al-rahim). It falls under good conduct, but it was singled out for mention out of concern for it and as an encouragement to do good to them. Al-fahsha' is adultery, or what its ugliness is manifest among sins. Its doer is always concealed in it, or it is the abomination of an act or statement, or stinginess, or what requires the prescribed punishment in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, or transgressing the limits of Allah. These are opinions, the first of which is from Ibn Abbas. Al-munkar is polytheism according to Muqatil, or what has been promised the Fire according to Ibn al-Sa'ib, or the contradiction between inner and outer conduct according to Ibn Uyaynah, or what does not require a prescribed punishment in this world but does bring punishment in the Hereafter, or what the intellects reject. These are opinions. It appears that it is more general than al-fahsha', since it includes sins, vices, and wrongdoing. Al-baghy is arrogance through injustice and seeking to achieve it. It falls under al-munkar, and it was singled out for mention out of concern for avoiding it. In what is commanded and what is forbidden, he combined what is obligatory and recommended, and what is forbidden and disliked, because they share a common element, which is the demand in the command and the abandonment in the prohibition. (p. 530)

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He commanded three things and forbade three things. Justice ('adl) is the middle path between excess (ifrat) and deficiency (tafrit), and this applies to beliefs ('aqa'id) and to the religious duties of the servants (a'mal al-ru'a).

Ibn 'Abbas said: Justice is "There is no god but God" (la ilaha illa Allah). It affirms one God, so it is neither pure negation of God (ta'til mahd) nor affirmation of more than one god. Affirming that He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful, with necessary attributes (wajib al-sifat), is not a denial of attributes, nor does it affirm an attribute that is newly originated and changing. The fact that a servant's act occurs through God's power and the motive (da'iyah) He placed in him is not pure compulsion (jabr mahd), nor is it the servant's independent possession of the act. That God brings out of the Fire whoever among the people of monotheism (ahl al-tawhid) entered it is not irja' (postponement of judgment regarding sinners), nor is it eternal punishment (takhlid) for sin.

As for the religious duties of the servants: the obligations (taklif) incumbent on them are not a claim that there is no obligation. Nor is it a claim of tormenting oneself and avoiding what the natural disposition inclines toward, such as eating good food, marrying, throwing oneself from a high place, and retaliation (qisas), blood-money (diyah), or pardon ('afw). It is not an excessive strictness in fixing retaliation as in the law of Moses, peace be upon him, nor an absolute, mandatory pardon as in the law of Jesus, peace be upon him. Avoiding a menstruating woman only in the matter of sexual intercourse is not total avoidance as in the law of Moses, peace be upon him, nor is intercourse with her during menstruation permitted as in the law of Jesus, peace be upon him. And circumcision (ikhtitan) is not leaving the foreskin (qulfah) intact, nor cutting off the organ, as the Manichaeans held.

God says: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾ [2:143]; ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾ [25:67]. Do not make the two verses [identical].

It is well known that they say: "By justice the heavens and the earth stand." Its meaning: if the proportions of the elements were not balanced, and some of them were greater, excess would prevail and the natures would be reversed. If the sun came close to the world, the heat would become enormous and everything in it would burn; and if it were farther away, heat and cold would become equal. Likewise are the measures of the movements of the stars and the degrees of their speed and slowness.

Ihsan (excellence) is exceeding what is obligatory in acts of obedience, in quantity and quality, in motives and in restraints, and in total immersion in witnessing the stations of servanthood ('ubudiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah). Among ihsan is compassion (shafaqah) toward creation, its root being maintaining ties of kinship (silat al-rahim). The forbidden thing is three.

That is because He placed in the human soul four powers: the appetitive power (shahwaniyyah), which is the pursuit of pleasures; the irascible power (ghadabiyyah), which is inflicting harm; and the imaginative power (wahmiyyah), which is satanic and strives for haughtiness and dominance over people. So indecency (fahsha') is what arises from the appetitive power when it goes beyond the discipline of the Sharia; the reprehensible (munkar) is what arises from the irascible power; and transgression (baghy) is what arises from the imaginative power. End of his words, that which was extracted from his speech; may God pardon him.

When God had commanded those three and forbidden those three, He said: ﴿He admonishes you with it﴾, meaning: with what He mentioned of command and prohibition. The meaning is: He alerts you in the best way, ﴿that you may remember﴾, that is, that you may be alert to what you were commanded and forbidden. The "covenant of God" (ahd Allah) is knowledge of what a person has pledged and bound himself to, from what agrees with the Sharia.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is the pledge of allegiance (bay'ah) to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to Islam: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you do but pledge allegiance to God﴾ [48:10]. It seems he had in mind what was said: that it was revealed concerning those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to Islam; this was narrated from Buraydah.

Qatadah and Mujahid said: It refers to what was among the alliances of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) in matters of enjoining good or forbidding evil.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: It is fidelity to whomever you have made a covenant with, whether Muslim or disbeliever, for the covenant is due to God.

Al-Asamm said: It is jihad and what has been obligated concerning wealth as a right.

It was also said: it is the oath by God. ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾: He forbade breaking them after they had been confirmed, meaning: after they were affirmed by the name of God, His guarantee, His witnessing, and His oversight, because the guarantor watches over the state of the one he guarantees.

﴿And do not be like a woman who unravels her thread after it has been spun, into pieces﴾, that is: in breaking the covenant after confirming it by God, be not like the foolish (wahra') woman who spins thread and then unravels it into strands (nakthan), which is what is undone of its twisting. The comparison does not require specifying the one compared to.

Al-Suddi and 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: she was a foolish woman in Mecca. From al-Kalbi and Muqatil: she was from Quraysh, a clumsy woman named Rayta daughter of Sa'd ibn Taym, nicknamed Jafra'. She used a spindle the length of a forearm, a whorl the size of a finger, and a large spindle-disc in proportion to them. She and her maidservants would spin from morning until noon, then she would order them and they would unravel what they had spun.

From Mujahid: this is the practice of the women of Najd, where one of them unravels her yarn, then fluffs it, mixes it with wool, and spins it again.

Ibn al-Anbari said: Rayta daughter of 'Amr al-Murriyyah, whose nickname was al-Jafra', from the people of Mecca; she was well known to the addressees.

The apparent meaning of His words ﴿after strength﴾ is: after a power (shiddah) that came about from the twisting of the strands of the thread. If we took it as a single strand, it would not unravel into pieces. Nakth in the language is the rope when its strands come apart.

Mujahid said: The meaning is "after a strand has been twisted into strength."

Al-Dakhal means corruption and deceit (al-daghal). They made faith a means to deception and treachery, because the one to whom the oath is sworn feels secure, so the swearer can harm him with what he wants. They said: it was revealed concerning the Arabs who, when they allied with a tribe and another larger group came, they would ally with the larger group and betray the smaller one.

It was also said: "Because one nation is more numerous than another" (an takuna antum azyada khabaran), where the verb is attributed to a nation (ummah), and the intended meaning is the addressees.

Ibn Bahr said: al-dakhal and the one who enters into a thing without being part of it; "dakhalan" is the second object (maf'ul thani).

It was also said: it is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), and "an takuna" means: because of [the fact] that it is. "Hiya arba" is a subject and predicate.

The Kufans permitted that "hiya" be an 'imad (a pronoun of separation, which they call fasl), so that "arba" would be in the accusative position. This is not permitted according to the Basrans because "ummah" is indefinite.

The pronoun in "bihi" refers to the verbal noun formed from "an takuna": that is, because of the fact that one nation is more numerous than another, He tests you by it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: so that He may see whether you hold fast to the rope of fidelity to the covenant of God and to what you have bound upon yourselves and confirmed with the oaths of the allegiance to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, or whether you are deceived by the multitude of Quraysh, their wealth, their strength, and the paucity, poverty, and weakness of the believers. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you﴾: a warning and caution against opposing the religion of Islam. End of his words.

It was also said: it refers to fidelity to the covenant. Ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Sa'ib, and Muqatil said: it refers to the multitude.

Ibn al-Anbari said: since its feminine form is not a true feminine, it was treated according to the sense of the masculine, just as "al-sayhah" (the cry) is treated according to the sense of "al-siyah" (the shouting).

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 16, verses 90–92 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to close relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may remember.﴾ ﴿Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make a pledge, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, although you have made Allah your guarantor over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And do not be like her who unravels her yarn after it has been strong, into broken threads, taking your oaths as means of deceit between you, because one community is more numerous than another. Allah only tests you thereby, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ.﴾ ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 93] ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was firmly planted, and you taste evil for having averted [others] from the way of Allah, and you will have a great punishment.﴾ [An-Nahl: 94] ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. What is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [An-Nahl: 95] ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah remains. And We will surely reward those who were patient with the best of what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 96] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nahl: 97] ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.﴾ [An-Nahl: 98] ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.﴾ [An-Nahl: 99] ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾ [An-Nahl: 100] ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, "You are only a fabricator." The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [An-Nahl: 103]

Al-a'jami is one who does not speak Arabic. (p. 529)

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to close relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may remember.﴾ ﴿Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make a pledge, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, although you have made Allah your guarantor over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And do not be like her who unravels her yarn after it has been strong, into broken threads, taking your oaths as means of deceit between you, because one community is more numerous than another. Allah only tests you thereby, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ.﴾: From Ibn Abbas, in a lengthy narration: "Uthman ibn Maz'un was a companion of the Prophet ﷺ for a time, and he said to him: 'Uthman, I have not seen you do your act this morning?' He said: 'And what did you see me do?' He said: 'Your gaze was lifted toward the sky, then you placed it on your right, and you turned away from me toward it and left me. Then you began nodding your head as if you were understanding something being said to you.' He said: 'Did you notice that? The Messenger of Allah came to me just now while you were sitting.' He said: 'What did he say to you?' He said to me: '﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾,' the verse. Uthman said: 'That was the moment when faith settled in my heart, and I came to love Muhammad ﷺ.'"
